title: Why Jesus Cooked Breakfast — John 21:12
paragraphs: He denied Jesus by a fire.
So Jesus rebuilt him… by another fire.
That’s not random. That’s redemption with precision.
In John 21, the risen Christ doesn’t summon Peter with thunder. He doesn’t interrogate him with shame. He cooks.
Bread. Fish. Fire crackling in the quiet morning.
The same Peter who cursed, who swore “I don’t know Him,” who ran when it mattered most… is now being served by the very Savior he abandoned.

Jesus wasn’t just feeding hunger.
He was restoring identity.

That charcoal fire?
It echoes the fire of Peter’s failure (John 18:18).
Failure met him there the first time.
Now grace meets him in the same place.

Because Jesus doesn’t erase your past by ignoring it.
He redeems it by revisiting it—with mercy.

And after every answer, Jesus responds:
“Feed My sheep.”

“You’re still called.
You’re still Mine.
I’m not done with you.”
Jesus cooked breakfast not because Peter deserved it…

You fail.
You fall.
You run.
But Jesus prepares a table anyway.

Repentance doesn’t earn the meal.
It leads you back to the One who already made it.
So if you’ve been avoiding God because of what you did—
And the table is still set.

From denial to breakfast.
From failure to calling.
